The project has a duration of 3 years and will run from October 2024 to September 2027. It has a budget of EUR 9.7 million and it builds on the experience and work done by previous technical assistance projects. The objective of ISPH II is to improve the conditions for better access to social protection and quality-assured health services in Cambodia in terms of climate adaptation, inclusion and gender equality. By improving the conditions for better access to social protection and quality-assured health services in Cambodia, the project hence contributes to the Cambodian Sustainable Development Goals (CSDG), in particular CSDGs 1.3.1 (social protection), 3.9 (social protection in the event of illness) and 3.c.1 (training of health workers). The project works actively with the General Secretariat of the National Social Protection Council (GS-NSPC) as its main counterpart. It also works with other actors of the social protection and health system, e.g. Ministry of Planning (IDPoor), National Social Assistance Fund, National Social Security Fund, Social Security Regulator, Ministry of Social Affairs, Veterans and Youth Rehabilitation, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Women Affairs, National Committee for Disaster Management, Ministry of Health, National Payment and Certification Agency, Health Science Institute of the Cambodian Armed Forces, Khmer-Soviet-Friendship-Hospital, Cambodian-Chinese-Friendship-Hospital. The project focuses on policy and capacity development. The project works on two intervention areas, social protection and health. Output 1 aims to strengthen the technical prerequisites for the further development of the social protection system, taking into account gender responsiveness and resilience to crises, in particular related to climate change. The aim of Output 2 is to strengthen institutional capacities for the implementation of social protection programmes, for example with regard to the introduction of mechanisms to review and/or optimise the climate and crisis response capacity. Output 3 aims to create selected technical prerequisites for improving access to social health protection, taking into account the needs of women and people with disabilities. This includes generation of evidence for policy decision as well as institutional strengthening. Output 4 aims to improve institutional capacities for quality-assured competence-based training of health professionals. This includes the development of competency-based curricula, the development of necessary individual competencies and the adaptation of training processes according to the standards and framework curricula provided for the competence-based training of medical professionals.
